title: Paramount C.E.O. Promises Editorial Independence for ‘60 Minutes’
partialText: David Ellison told Lesley Stahl, one of three remaining correspondents for the news program, that he would respect the show’s editorial decisions after a tumultuous stretch.

title: Social Security Benefits Could Be Cut in 6 Years Unless Congress Acts
partialText: The trust fund for the program, which supports roughly 68 million Americans, is on schedule to be depleted in the next six years. Benefits could be cut on average by 22 percent.

title: Billionaires’ Billions Are Increasing Faster Than Ever
partialText: Elon Musk’s potential new status as a trillionaire demonstrates in real time why there has been such a rapid rise in the concentration of wealth at the top.

title: Dutch Authorities Block $115 Million Deal by a U.S. Tech Company
partialText: The Netherlands blocked a U.S. company from buying a Dutch firm that handles its national ID system, saying it would create a “threat to the public interest.”

title: Why Apple’s A.I. Upgrade for Siri Won’t Be Available in Europe
partialText: A regulatory dispute has indefinitely delayed the release of Siri AI.

title: U.S. Exports Rose in April, as War with Iran Buoyed Oil Demand
partialText: Commerce Department data showed exports rose in April, slightly outpacing the growth in imports.

title: OpenAI Tests Investor Appetite for Yet Another Giant I.P.O.
partialText: Some analysts are wondering whether the market can absorb the artificial intelligence giant’s planned stock offering — along with those of SpaceX and Anthropic.

title: Stocks Drop on Tech Fears and War Worries
partialText: Oil prices fell after Israel and Iran agreed to halt strikes against each other, easing fears of a broader regional conflict that had briefly driven crude higher.

title: Dubai’s Economic Endurance Is Being Tested in War With Iran
partialText: As conflict ripples through the Persian Gulf, Dubai’s dependence on trade and travel has become an economic vulnerability.

title: As Screwworm Cases Mount, U.S. Officials Ramp Up Response
partialText: The parasitic, flesh-eating fly has now been confirmed in cows, goats and dogs.

title: Hoyle Schweitzer, Who Brought Windsurfing to the Masses, Dies at 93
partialText: With his friend Jim Drake, he built the Windsurfer, a sailboard that was cheaper and more portable than most sailboats. It became a global phenomenon.

title: How Banks Are Using the SpaceX IPO to Woo the Super Rich
partialText: Wall Street is giving its richest clients velvet rope access to this week’s public listing of SpaceX, reflecting the growing importance of the wealth management business.

title: The Iran War is Forcing Energy-Importing Countries to Turn Inward
partialText: The Iran war is pushing countries to prioritize domestic energy in order to protect themselves from volatile oil and natural gas markets.

title: Trump Eyes a Piece of A.I. Giants
partialText: The president has publicly weighed the government taking stakes in artificial intelligence giants, as his position on regulating the industry shifts.

title: Europe Watches Its Economic Recovery Fade Into the Distance
partialText: As the war in Iran persists, signs point to a prolonged period of higher prices and slower growth rather than a quick shock.

title: Have a Thorny Medical Question? Your Doctor May Be Using A.I. for That.
partialText: OpenEvidence, a fast-growing start-up, is using artificial intelligence to help doctors find answers to clinical questions for diagnosis and treatment.

title: Oil Rises as Hostilities Escalate Between Iran and Israel
partialText: Oil prices jumped and stocks plunged after Iran and Israel exchanged strikes, raising doubts about the future of fragile cease-fire in the Middle East.

title: Kars4Kids Can Continue Broadcasting Ads in California, Appeals Court Says
partialText: A lower court last month found that the ads from the charity, known for its ear-worm jingle, had violated false-advertising laws.

title: ‘Scary Movie’ Returns Politically Incorrect Humor to Top of the Box Office
partialText: The film took in $55 million over the weekend in the United States and Canada. It was the biggest opening for an R-rated comedy in 12 years.

title: 5 Takeaways From Scott Pelley’s Interview With The New York Times
partialText: Mr. Pelley, who was at CBS News for 37 years, including as a White House correspondent and a “60 Minutes” correspondent, spoke in his first extended interview since he was fired.

title: OPEC Plus to Boost Oil Production as Ceasefire in Iran Remains Elusive
partialText: The cartel’s move to increase output by 188,000 barrels per day is largely symbolic, with vast amounts of the world’s oil stranded by the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: How People Working in Debt Collection Handle Abuse From Callers
partialText: More Americans are taking on debt and falling behind on bills. The people calling them to collect often endure a torrent of verbal abuse and threats of violence.

title: My Boss Is a Manipulative Creep. What Can I Do?
partialText: Plus: How much unpaid work can a recruiter demand? And what on earth is that smell?

title: Daughter of Mrs. Fields Starts Fields Good, a Healthy Cookie Brand
partialText: Ashley Fields is a co-founder of Fields Good cookies. One variety contains protein, and others claim to boost brain performance or aid sleep.

title: As Oil Prices Spike, Talk of ‘Demand Destruction’ Sets In
partialText: The decades-old term refers to the sustained loss of demand for a commodity, caused by high prices.

title: Christine Hunsicker, CaaStle CEO, Confessed to Fraud. The Board Let Her Stay in Charge.
partialText: The final months of the fashion tech start-up CaaStle included fake audits, stock buybacks and a damage control strategy led by the chief executive who defrauded it.

title: Alan Riding, Times Correspondent in Latin America and Paris, Dies at 82
partialText: He was a cosmopolitan observer and interpreter of societies he knew firsthand, whether writing about war in Nicaragua or the history and cultural salons of France.

title: ‘Talk to My A.I. Twin’: Busy Executives Have a New Productivity Hack
partialText: C.E.O.s and Harvard professors ae making A.I.-powered doubles that answer questions and attend meetings.

title: Screwworm Flies Add to Cattle Ranchers’ Woes
partialText: Some Texans fear “the nightmares and the horrors” of a potential screwworm outbreak. Elsewhere, not enough grass to feed cattle sends them to market earlier.

title: ‘60 Minutes’ Is a ‘Cage Full of Tigers.’ Can Nick Bilton Lead It?
partialText: The tech journalist and filmmaker was a surprise choice to lead a famously combative newsroom. His first week was chaos.

title: 5 Tips to Start Managing Your Aging Parents’ Money
partialText: And one big mistake to avoid.

title: Stocks Slide as Investors See Rates Rising After Strong Jobs Data
partialText: The S&P 500 fell more than 2.6 percent on Friday, its worst one-day drop of the year and ending nine weeks of gains.

title: ’60 Minutes’ Stars Will Stay After Pelley’s Firing Because They Don’t Want Show to ‘Die’
partialText: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim said on Friday in an email to the show’s staff that they had reached the decision after a period of “grieving” and frustration.

title: What to know about the report.
Central Ohio Becomes Hub for Tech and Manufacturing
partialText: Tech titans and Silicon Valley transplants changed the Columbus area, but not everyone is thrilled about the rapid transformation.

title: Elon Musk Dominates List of Highest Paid C.E.O.s
partialText: Executive compensation is accelerating while rank-and-file workers lag, widening the pay gap in corporate America.

title: White House rejoices over strong jobs report.
partialText: The stronger-than-expected report offers President Trump a talking point for the midterms, even as it also reduces the odds that the Federal Reserve may cut rates.

title: More Renters Are Using Tools to Skip Security Deposits, but There’s a Catch
partialText: Third-party services charge fees to help renters bypass some upfront costs of signing a lease. Unlike traditional deposits, the money won’t be returned to tenants.

title: Anthropic’s Call for A.I. Nonproliferation
partialText: The artificial intelligence giant said a “brake pedal” was needed to protect humanity from self-improving models. The proposal could have big consequences.

title: With Jobs Market Stable, Fed Is Focusing on Inflation Over Rate Cuts
partialText: Officials at the Federal Reserve have turned their focus to resurgent inflation.

title: U.S. Job Market Pushes Past Shocks and Strains
partialText: Employers added 172,000 jobs in May, adding to a vigorous pace of hiring in recent months. But wage growth is not keeping up with higher prices and consumers remain pessimistic.

title: How the Job Market Is Leaving New Graduates Behind
partialText: Sydney Ember, a Times business reporter, has been speaking with recent college graduates struggling to find work. She explains why starting a career in the current economy could leave lasting scars on wages and opportunities.

title: To Sell Trucks, Break Out the Cowboys and Wrap Them in Old Glory
partialText: Americans — especially American men — love trucks, and high gas prices aren’t swaying automakers. Ram has a new line of fuel-guzzling muscle trucks, and some in-your-face ads to sell them.

title: Crowded Airport Lounges Are Rolling Out Grab-and-Go Options
partialText: New premium pit stops are giving fliers a place for a quick bite and drink without having to line up for increasingly crowded traditional lounges.

title: Can He-Man’s ‘Masters of the Universe’ Generate the Same Movie Magic as Barbie?
partialText: “Masters of the Universe” will test whether Mattel can cement itself as an entertainment powerhouse with a hypermasculine character from the 1980s.

title: A Job Market Leaving Young Graduates Behind Could Scar Them for Years
partialText: The labor market has improved, but people entering the work force are having a harder time starting careers, a dynamic that has had permanent effects in the past.

title: When Jeffrey Epstein Needed Favors, This Restaurant Mogul Was There
partialText: Stephen Hanson, whose empire included Blue Water Grill and Ruby Foo’s, was a devoted friend and wingman who helped manage and entertain the women in Epstein’s orbit.

title: China Builds an Economic Fortress as Global Tensions Rise
partialText: Beijing says the changes are needed for national security, but they could complicate efforts by Chinese companies to find growth overseas.

title: Nick Bilton, New ‘60 Minutes’ Chief, Pledges Independence
partialText: Nick Bilton said he had consulted with the program’s remaining correspondents: Lesley Stahl, Jon Wertheim and Bill Whitaker. All three were deliberating whether to stay with the show, two people said.
